channel.title: Carbon Energy Nexus
channel.description: Sourced daily intelligence on carbon, energy, water and capital.

item.title: IEA raises its 2050 carbon removal need by 30% as operating capture capacity sits at 68 Mt a year
item.description: 30% more carbon removal by 2050: that is the IEA's new net zero need, with 6.4 billion tonnes of CO2 captured a year against 68 million tonnes of capacity running today.

item.title: Australia agrees to store Singapore's CO2 as Gorgon injected only 26% of its separated CO2 last year
item.description: Canberra, Nov 24: Singapore and Australia signed a treaty to ship CO2 captured in Singapore to offshore storage under Australian jurisdiction, as Gorgon data shows only 26% of its separated CO2 was injected last year.

item.title: US data centers have announced more than 115 GW of their own gas plants, enough to add 152 Mt of CO2 a year
item.description: Data centers want power fast, but the fastest route is gas. US campuses have announced more than 115 GW of on-site gas plants, which BloombergNEF says could add 152 Mt of CO2 a year versus the grid.

item.title: Congo will halt cobalt exports again from Nov 30 as prices slide and stockpiles build
item.description: 96,600 tonnes was Congo's 2026 cobalt export ceiling. From Nov 30 the quota gives way to a full suspension with no end date, as prices slide and inventories build, the regulator said.

item.title: COP31 ends without a deal, and its carbon capture and electrification goals fall with it
item.description: Two extra days in Antalya, but no cover decision. COP31 closed on Sunday after the EU and others rejected a text that named no fossil fuels, taking a draft 500 Mt a year capture goal and a 35% electrification target with it.

item.title: The bigger water bill behind new data centers is at the power plant, Western estimates show
item.description: 22,000 acre-feet a year. That is the water Nevada researchers tie to generating power for planned data centers, more than the sites would use directly, as utilities and auditors start pricing data center water.

item.title: The EU and UK agree to link their carbon markets, with cross-border CO2 storage next in line
item.description: The EU and UK agreed on Nov 20 to link their carbon markets from 2028, recognizing each other's allowances and exempting traded goods from carbon border charges. Industry says cross-border CO2 storage could cut costs by up to 28%.

item.title: COP31's new draft drops fossil fuel language but keeps a carbon capture goal
item.description: COP31's second draft deal, released Nov 19, removes every direct reference to fossil fuels but keeps a goal of at least 500 million tonnes of carbon capture a year by 2035, still in brackets, and a 35% electrification target.

item.title: COP31's draft deal asks the world to build 500 million tonnes of carbon capture by 2035
item.description: COP31's first draft deal asks countries to scale carbon capture to at least 500 million tonnes a year by 2035. The world runs about 68 million today. The EU and a bloc including Saudi Arabia and India want changes before talks close Nov 20.

item.title: Europe hands heavy industry more free carbon permits as COP31 enters its final week
item.description: EU governments and Parliament agreed on Nov 12 to give energy-intensive industry roughly 121 million more free carbon permits through 2030. Allowances traded near €90 a tonne, but a softer long-run price weakens the case for carbon capture and shifts cost to taxpayers.
